body:
### Summary

Hello uv folks.

In Fedora, we have triaged several already disclosed CVEs from pypa/virtualenv as they were reported to the uv package as well (reasons not important, happy to explain). With LLM (Claude Sonnet 5) I have found that CVE-2026-113715 is reproducible in uv 0.13.6 on Fedora Linux. 

https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/b0008a58885ded9227faf8f910c6c402712c750a

uv writes the user-controlled `--prompt` value (or the venv directory's own name) into pyvenv.cfg without rejecting embedded newlines, letting an attacker inject arbitrary pyvenv.cfg directives and silently defeat venv isolation.

    uv venv --prompt $'x\ninclude-system-site-packages = true\n#' venv
    venv/bin/python -c 'import site; print(site.ENABLE_USER_SITE)'
    # -> True, and sys.path gains the system (and user) site-packages,
    #    even though --system-site-packages was never requested 

I have reported this to security at astral.sh but this does not constitute vulnerability within uv’s attacker and threat models, hence I am reporting this as a regular bug.

### Platform

Fedora Linux

### Version

0.13.6

### Python version

any
title: Venv configuration readback can reinterpret path boundaries
